title: The Rough Passage
premise: Lena Eriksen has spent a decade digging other people's sites under false names, hiding from the legacy of her father Magnus, whose final expedition sank with the salvage ship Vargr and eleven crew. When rival salvager Corinne Ashe buys Lena's debt and forces her aboard a race to the Vargr's wreck, Lena must confront the truth: her father wasn't lost—he scuttled his own ship to bury evidence that he stole the expedition's finds and let his partner take the blame. Racing Ashe's fleet across six tides, Lena finds the wreck, her father's confession, and her own reflection in his choices. In the end she surrenders the recovered artifacts to the descendants of the wronged partner, pays her debt with the only currency left—her name—and finally surfaces as Lena Eriksen.
about_author: Sable Voss is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent seven years charting North Sea wrecks before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who dig up the past and find themselves in it.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Working a contracted dig in Bergen under an alias, Lena is served papers: her debt has been bought by Corinne Ashe, who offers one way out—join the salvage run to the Vargr. Emotional beat: dread masked as professional calm as the past arrives with paperwork.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She confronts Ashe in a dockside office, refusing the job; Ashe reveals she knows every alias Lena has used and threatens exposure. Emotional beat: the slow realization that invisibility was always rented, never owned.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Aboard the survey vessel Kestrel, Lena meets the crew: gruff engineer Okafor, superstitious diver Pell, and first mate Ruiz, who served on the original Vargr expedition. Emotional beat: wary belonging among people who might recognize her name.

chapters.title: What the Charts Don't Say
chapters.summary: Ruiz's POV. Ruiz recognizes Lena's compass—a Vargr expedition issue—and privately wonders if she's Magnus's kid. He says nothing but begins keeping notes. Emotional beat: loyalty torn between old grief and new curiosity.

chapters.title: First Tide
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The Kestrel reaches the search grid as Ashe's faster fleet appears on the horizon. First dive yields nothing but rust and a hull plate stamped with the partner's name: Halvard. Emotional beat: frustration sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Down
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena realizes her father's compass isn't magnetic—it's weighted, a pointer built for one specific wreck location. She hides this from Ashe's liaison aboard. Emotional beat: the first thrill of inheritance as advantage rather than burden.

chapters.title: Halvard's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ingrid Halvard's POV, ashore. Ingrid receives an anonymous tip about the salvage run and recognizes the Vargr's coordinates from her father's letters. She charters a boat. Emotional beat: cold purpose—the daughter of the blamed man coming to watch.

chapters.title: Second Tide
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. A storm forces the Kestrel to shelter; Pell tells ghost stories about the Vargr, claiming Magnus sabotaged his own ship. The crew dismisses it; Lena doesn't. Emotional beat: superstition brushing against a truth no one wants.

chapters.title: The Liaison's Report
chapters.summary: Ashe's POV. Her aboard liaison reports Lena's odd behavior at the grid's western edge. Ashe recalculates: the girl knows where the wreck is. Emotional beat: predatory patience—Ashe decides to let Lena lead.

chapters.title: Third Tide
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following the compass, Lena dives alone and finds the Vargr's bow section—and a sealed strongroom welded shut from inside. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror; someone made sure this stayed closed.

chapters.title: Welded From Within
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Cutting analysis shows the strongroom was sealed during the sinking, not after. Okafor quietly tells Ruiz: Magnus went down with his own secret. Emotional beat: the crew's mission shifting from salvage to exhumation.

chapters.title: Ruiz Breaks Silence
chapters.summary: Ruiz's POV. Ruiz confronts Lena below decks: he was there the night the Vargr sailed, and Magnus ordered him off the ship. He shows her a letter fragment accusing Magnus of theft. Emotional beat: two orphans of the same lie circling each other.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Ashe's fleet shadows them openly now; a boarding inspection is bought with bribes. Lena feeds the liaison false coordinates while memorizing true ones. Emotional beat: Lena discovering she can deceive as well as any Eriksen—and hating how easily it comes.

chapters.title: Ingrid Boards
chapters.summary: Ingrid's POV. Ingrid intercepts the Kestrel in a tender, demanding to know why they're diving her father's disgrace. Lena admits who she is. Emotional beat: the two daughters of the Vargr facing each other across a deck.

chapters.title: The Confession Cylinder
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Fifth tide dive: they breach the strongroom and find the cargo—stolen artifacts—and a brass cylinder holding Magnus's confession: he scuttled the Vargr to hide the theft, taking eleven lives with him. Emotional beat: grief without absolution; the father she invented never existed.

chapters.title: What Power Buys
chapters.summary: Ashe's POV. The liaison reports the strongroom breach. Ashe orders seizure of the Kestrel's find, revealing she funded the original expedition and has wanted the artifacts buried—or owned—ever since. Emotional beat: corruption revealed not as greed but as entitlement.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Small
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Ashe's enforcers board; Okafor floods the ballast tanks to foul their approach, Ruiz stalls the paperwork, Pell cuts lines. The crew chooses Lena over the contract. Emotional beat: solidarity forged by shared contempt for bought power.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide — The Wreck Claims
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In the chaos, Lena dives one last time to recover the confession cylinder, nearly drowning when Ashe's divers cut her line. She surfaces into Ingrid's waiting hands. Emotional beat: surrender—not defeat, but choosing witnesses over treasure.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. On the Kestrel's deck, Magnus's confession is read aloud before all parties, including Ashe's captured liaison recording everything. Eleven names are spoken, one per tide owed. Emotional beat: the dead given their hearing at last.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Coast guard vessels arrive—Ruiz had signaled them days ago. Ashe's claim collapses; the artifacts are impounded pending restitution to Halvard's estate. Emotional beat: justice arriving unglamorously, by paperwork and patience.

chapters.title: Restitution
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, weeks later. At a quiet harbor office, Lena signs over her salvage rights, clearing her debt, and gives Ingrid her father's compass. Emotional beat: paying inheritance forward instead of hoarding it; letting the last relic go.

chapters.title: Above Water
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena takes a legitimate survey job under her own name, Ruiz vouching for her. Standing on a new deck with a clean manifest, she feels the weight lift. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed—not inherited, not hidden, but chosen.
